episode_title: Customers Ask the Same Questions Every Day with AI for Dental Office

real_qa.q: What are the four-week pilot sequence steps recommended in the Grow with Technology AI for Dental Offices report to safely introduce AI into a dental practice?
real_qa.r: Week one establishes baseline with narrow scope, maybe only web chat. Week two is a stress test where staff deliberately try to break the AI by asking it to book appointments for dogs, using slang, and asking it to diagnose rashes. Week three is controlled launch with real patients while staff monitors closely. Week four is decision time comparing outcomes to baseline data to decide whether to revise, expand, or pull the plug entirely.
real_qa.requete: Grow with Technology four week pilot dental AI

real_qa.q: What is confabulation according to NIST in the context of AI in healthcare, and why is it dangerous for dental practices?
real_qa.r: Confabulation, according to the National Institute of Standards and Technology, is when AI makes things up and presents those errors with absolute, unwavering confidence. It is dangerous because it encourages misplaced trust—if an AI confidently assures a patient that a complex surgery is fully covered by a basic insurance plan, the patient will believe it and then get a massive bill later.

real_qa.q: Why must AI in dental offices be restricted to an approved content library rather than having open web access, and what documentation must be maintained?
real_qa.r: The AI must be restricted to an approved content library of exactly 10 frequent questions with rigorous documentation. For every single fact, you record the source document, the named employee who approved it, the exact approval date, and a calendar trigger for review. You keep strict version history so if the AI gives a weird answer, staff can see exactly which approved text the AI pulled from.
real_qa.requete: dental AI content library approved documentation

real_qa.q: What is a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and how does it apply to dental practices using AI chatbots that handle patient health information?
real_qa.r: A BAA is a legally binding contract that transfers liability and forces the tech company to adhere to the same strict privacy standards as the doctor. It dictates what happens if there is a data breach and creates a legal chain of custody. If a cloud software vendor is handling transcripts, analyzing call data, or touching electronic protected health information on behalf of the practice, that vendor is legally classified as a business associate and requires a BAA.
real_qa.requete: Business Associate Agreement BAA dental HIPAA

real_qa.q: How should dental practices calculate the actual return on investment (ROI) when implementing AI for front desk operations if staff salaries remain unchanged?
real_qa.r: The calculation reveals capacity saved, not immediate cash. If 30 routine inquiries at 2 minutes each equals 20 hours monthly, and AI resolves half, you free 10 hours at a $30 loaded labor cost, equaling $300 monthly value. After subtracting $200 software costs, the ROI is reallocation: staff use those 10 freed hours following up on unpaid insurance claims or explaining complex treatment plans to hesitant patients, generating real revenue.
real_qa.requete: dental AI ROI calculation staff capacity reallocation
